MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about 90 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is even because it ends in 0
   B. It is odd because it ends in 0
   C. It is odd because it has an even number of digits
   D. It is neither even nor odd

2. Which of these is a multiple of 5? (1 mark)
   A. 65
   B. 64
   C. 67
   D. 66

3. Which of these is a factor of 36? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 7

4. Which word in a problem tells you to add? (1 mark)
   A. Fewer
   B. Remain
   C. Difference
   D. Altogether

5. Work out 3,425 + 2,318. (1 mark)
   A. 5,743
   B. 5,733
   C. 5,753
   D. 5,643

6. What is the rule of the pattern 2,000, 2,500, 3,000, 3,500? (1 mark)
   A. add 2,000
   B. subtract 500
   C. add 500
   D. add 1,000

7. A tank held 8,000 litres of water. The school used 3,450 litres. How many litres are left? (1 mark)
   A. 4,550 litres
   B. 4,540 litres
   C. 4,650 litres
   D. 5,450 litres

8. Work out 7,300 − 4,562. (1 mark)
   A. 2,738
   B. 2,638
   C. 3,262
   D. 2,748

9. Work out 18 × 35. (1 mark)
   A. 630
   B. 144
   C. 620
   D. 640

10. What is 63 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 18,900
   B. 189
   C. 93
   D. 1,890

11. What is 35 × 60? (1 mark)
   A. 21,000
   B. 2,100
   C. 95
   D. 210

12. 47 mangoes are shared equally among 6 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 5
   C. 1
   D. 6

13. What is 500 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 50
   B. 6
   C. 5
   D. 500

14. 59 mangoes are shared equally among 8 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 3
   C. 7
   D. 4

15. Change 2 7/10 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 27/10
   B. 28/10
   C. 9/10
   D. 20/10

16. Dan writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 11/5
   B. 8/3
   C. 4 2/3
   D. 1/2

17. What is 7/10 of 20? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 6
   C. 16
   D. 14

18. Write 2 25/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 2.025
   B. 2.25
   C. 0.225
   D. 22.5

19. Write 0.09 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 90/100
   B. 9/100
   C. 9/1000
   D. 9/10

20. Write 27/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.27
   B. 2.7
   C. 0.027
   D. 0.72

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A trader sold goods worth Ksh 3,568 on Monday and Ksh 2,276 on Tuesday. (a) Find the total. (b) Estimate the total by rounding each amount to the nearest ten. (c) How far is the estimate from the exact total? (5 marks)

22. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250. (3 marks)

23. In the number 27,150, give the place value and the total value of the digit 7. (4 marks)

24. Mama Njoki has 24 oranges. She gives 3/8 of them to her neighbours and 1/4 of them to a friend. (a) How many oranges does she give to her neighbours? (b) How many does she give to her friend? (c) How many oranges are left? (5 marks)

25. Work out 12 × 21 showing both partial products. (3 marks)

26. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875. How many were left? Estimate first by rounding to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

27. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded and what fraction is not shaded? (2 marks)

28. Write 4,605 in words and 305 in words. Then say which is greater. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — It is even because it ends in 0
   Look at the ones digit. 0 is even, so 90 is even.

2. A — 65
   65 = 5 × 13, so 65 is a multiple of 5.

3. A — 9
   36 ÷ 9 = 4 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 36. The others leave a remainder.

4. D — Altogether
   Altogether means put the amounts together, so we add.

5. A — 5,743
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,425 + 2,318 = 5,743.

6. C — add 500
   Each number is 500 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 500.

7. A — 4,550 litres
   Subtract 8,000 − 3,450 = 4,550. Check by adding: 4,550 + 3,450 = 8,000.

8. A — 2,738
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,300 − 4,562 = 2,738. Check: 2,738 + 4,562 = 7,300.

9. A — 630
   18 × 5 = 90 and 18 × 30 = 540. 90 + 540 = 630.

10. D — 1,890
   63 × 3 = 189, then × 10 gives 1,890.

11. B — 2,100
   35 × 6 = 210, then × 10 gives 2,100.

12. B — 5
   47 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 5. Each child gets 7 and 5 are left.

13. C — 5
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 500 ÷ 100 = 5.

14. B — 3
   59 ÷ 8 = 7 remainder 3. Each child gets 7 and 3 are left.

15. A — 27/10
   2 × 10 = 20 and 20 + 7 = 27. The denominator stays 10, so the answer is 27/10.

16. C — 4 2/3
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 4 2/3.

17. D — 14
   20 ÷ 10 = 2 and 2 × 7 = 14. So 7/10 of 20 is 14.

18. B — 2.25
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 2 25/100 = 2.25.

19. B — 9/100
   The last digit of 0.09 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.09 = 9/100.

20. A — 0.27
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 27/100 = 0.27.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 5,844 (b) 3,570 + 2,280 = Ksh 5,850 (c) 6 shillings more than the exact total
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact total with regrouping, 1 mark for both rounded numbers, 1 mark for the estimate 5,850, 1 mark for the difference 5,850 − 5,844 = 6.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4,000, 3,750, 3,500 (rule: subtract 250)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three numbers.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Place value: thousands. Total value: 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for thousands; 1 mark for 7 × 1,000; 1 mark for the answer 7,000; 1 mark for clear working.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 9 oranges (b) 6 oranges (c) 9 oranges
   Working / marking points: (a) 24 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 3 = 9 (2 marks); (b) 24 ÷ 4 = 6 (1 mark); (c) 24 − 9 − 6 = 9 (2 marks).

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 252
   Working / marking points: 12 × 1 = 12 (1 mark); 12 × 20 = 240 (1 mark); 12 + 240 = 252 (1 mark).

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 6,500 − 2,880 = 3,620. Exact: 3,625 seedlings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding 2,875 to 2,880 (6,500 stays), 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for the exact working, 1 mark for the answer.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5/12 is shaded and 7/12 is not shaded.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5/12 and 1 mark for 12 − 5 = 7, so 7/12.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4,605 is four thousand, six hundred and five. 305 is three hundred and five. 4,605 is greater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct wording and 1 mark each for the comparison and its reason (more digits).
